sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent - State and perused the material on record 3.

The complaint is lodged by the victim stating that she is a permanent resident of Goa and after giving divorce to her husband, she was living alone and at that time, she came in contact with the petitioner and she is in live-in relationship with him.
It is alleged that on three occasions, she became pregnant and the petitioner gave some tablets and terminated the pregnancy.

It is further alleged that the petitioner had promised that he will marry her and collected about nine lakhs NC:
2023:KHC:21236 rupees and also gold ornaments from her but later, cheated her.

Further on 27.01.2023, he brought her from Goa to Bengaluru promising that he will introduce her to his parents and stayed in a lodge for three days but he did not take her to the house of his parents, but she was beaten and threatened by his relatives.
4. A perusal of the complaint averments reveal that since four years, victim and the petitioner are in a relationship.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that there is absolutely no material to show that a huge sum of Rs. 9 lakhs has been given by the victim to the petitioner and there is not even a single document in this regard produced before the Police at the time of lodging the complaint.
He contends that the entire allegations that the victim was beaten and threatened by the relatives of the petitioner are false.
5. According to the victim, the petitioner has cheated her by receiving Rs.9 lakhs and gold ornaments from her.
The same is a matter which has to be investigated and established during trial.
The incident of assault has taken place, according to the victim on 27.01.2023.
It is stated that on the same day, NC: 2023:KHC:21236 the Hoysala police have taken her to the Police Station.
The complaint sent to the Commissioner of Police is dated 14.02.2023.

sentences.text: Considering the above facts and circumstances, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted by imposing conditions.

Hence, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the petitioner/accused No.1 in Crime No.23/2023 of R.M.C.
Yard Police Station, he shall be released subject to following conditions:
a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with two sureties for the likesum.
b) Petitioner shall furnish proof of his address and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
NC: 2023:KHC:21236 c) Petitioner shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) Petitioner shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
If any of the above conditions are violated, prosecution is at liberty to seek cancellation of bail.
